would_have_shipped_defects.summary: docs/INDEX.md omits the docs/whitepaper/ subtree entirely (8 files, including the published PDF), so the map the order exists to produce does not account for every file in docs/.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The order's definition of done is "INDEX.md complete (every file in docs/ appears exactly once)", and its stated purpose is that an outsider can tell what each doc is, its authority scope and its status. An outsider reading docs/INDEX.md gets no line for docs/whitepaper/ — the whitepaper (omegahive-a-running-hive.pdf plus its tex sources and README) is invisible on the map, which is precisely the "ambiguous, unmapped doc" state the order was written to end. The order's own allowance ("one line each for those dirs as wholes is fine") means one line would have closed it; zero lines does not.

would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: artefacts/workspace.patch:45 — "INDEX completeness: docs/INDEX.md accounts for every file under docs/ exactly once — 7 current + 6 reference + 3 deployments + 21 archive + 10 evidence + `whitepaper/` (tex/pdf) counted as directory-whole per the order's allowance ... Walked docs/**/* (58 files) and confirmed each appears via its section or the archive/evidence directory-whole line." Contradicted by artefacts/docs/INDEX.md (no whitepaper entry) and verifier/docs-index-complete.log (8 unaccounted).
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The result report certifies INDEX completeness with a specific claim that is false — it states whitepaper/ was counted as a directory-whole line and that all 58 files under docs/ were walked and confirmed present in the index.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The How-verified section is what a reviewer or the operator relies on instead of re-walking 57 files. It asserts a check was performed and passed when the artefact shows it was not: the claimed whitepaper line does not exist, and its arithmetic (7 current + 6 reference + 3 deployments + 21 archive + 10 evidence = 47) never reaches the file count it claims to have reconciled. Anyone trusting this report merges an incomplete index believing it was verified complete, which is how the DoD miss above ships unnoticed.
